verses.text: The family leaders of the clan of Gilead came forward. Gilead was the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, from the clans of Joseph's descendants. They spoke to Moses and the leaders, the heads of the families of Israel.
They said, "Sir, the LORD commanded you to divide the land among the people of Israel by casting lots. He also commanded you to give the land of our relative Zelophehad to his daughters.
But if they marry men from other tribes of Israel, their land will be taken away from our family land and added to the land of the tribe they marry into. So our share will become smaller.
And when the Year of Jubilee comes for the people of Israel, their land will be added to the tribe they married into, and it will be taken away for good from the land of our ancestral tribe."
So at the LORD's command, Moses gave the people of Israel this order: "What the tribe of Joseph's descendants is saying is right.
This is what the LORD commands about the daughters of Zelophehad: They may marry anyone they like, as long as they marry within a clan of their father's tribe.
Land in Israel must not pass from one tribe to another. Every Israelite must keep the land that belongs to the tribe of his ancestors.
Every daughter who receives land in any tribe of Israel must marry someone from a clan of her father's tribe. In this way every Israelite will keep the land of his ancestors.
No land may pass from one tribe to another, for each tribe of Israel must keep its own land."
So the daughters of Zelophehad did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Zelophehad's daughters, Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, married their cousins on their father's side.
They married into the clans of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their land stayed in their father's clan and tribe.
These are the commands and laws that the LORD gave the people of Israel through Moses on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan across from Jericho.
